newsitem.title: USA: Ohio Casualty Q3 catastrophe losses.
newsitem.headline: Ohio Casualty Q3 catastrophe losses.

text.p: Ohio Casualty Corp said catastrophe losses in the quarter were $16.5 million, up from the $5.7 million in the same period a year ago.
Third quarter catastrophe losses contributed 5.5 points to the combined ratio in 1996 and 1.8 points in 1995.
The combined ratio for the quarter was 108.4 percent, up from a combined ratio of 103.3 percent in the 1995 third quarter.
The combined ratio indicates whether a company is earning a profit on the business it writes. An underwriting profit occurs when the ratio is below 100 percent.
Losses from Hurricanes Bertha and Fran totaled $9.1 million before taxes, including $1.5 million in windstorm pool assessments.
This represents 3.0 points on the third quarter combined ratio, Ohio Casualty said.
The company said third quarter net written premiums from property-casualty operations totaled $300.1 million, down 4.5 percent from the same period last year.
However, the company said it was important to note that premium from active agents was up 2.5 percent in the quarter compared with the same quarter last year.
